issues.t: Erratic or harsh shifting from the pressure control solenoid
issues.sym: The automatic shifts hard, flares or slips between gears, skips gears, or seems not to know which gear it should be in. A check engine light may come on.
issues.why: The pressure control solenoid inside the transmission wears out and can no longer control line pressure properly. It is the most-reported Intrigue problem on RepairPal.
issues.next: Have the transmission codes read and the fluid checked. Replacing the solenoid can fix it if done early; once clutches are burned, a rebuild is needed.

issues.t: Automatic transmission fails and needs a rebuild
issues.sym: Slipping, no engagement in some gears, or the car won't move, usually past 90,000 miles.
issues.why: Internal wear in the 4-speed automatic. Owners report full rebuilds around 90,000 to 110,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and color. If it slips or won't engage, stop driving it hard and get quotes from an independent transmission shop.

issues.t: Power steering pressure hose leaks
issues.sym: Power steering fluid drips under the front of the car, a whining pump, or steering that gets heavy, especially when parking.
issues.why: The high-pressure power steering hose leaks at its crimped fittings as it ages.
issues.next: Check the power steering fluid level. Running the pump dry ruins it, so have the leaking hose replaced soon.

issues.t: Steering becomes hard to turn left (recall)
issues.sym: Steering effort rises, especially in left turns, and at worst the wheel resists turning left and then the assist pushes right.
issues.why: Retainer tabs on the lower pinion bearing in the steering rack may not have been crimped properly, letting the bearing balls escape. GM recalled these cars (NHTSA 03V527).
issues.next: If steering effort changes, have it inspected right away. A dealer can check your VIN for this recall, which installs a new bearing or a whole new steering gear.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing hum or grinding
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that rises with speed and may change when you turn. Sometimes the ABS light comes on.
issues.why: The front hub-and-bearing assemblies wear out, often around 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Have both front hubs checked; when one goes, the other is often close. Replace the bad hub before it gets loose.

issues.t: Burns oil between changes
issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes, sometimes a quart a month, and you may see blue smoke from the tailpipe.
issues.why: Many 3.5L Twin Cam engines burn oil as they age. Owners also find leaking seals and gaskets. Running it low on oil can wreck the engine.
issues.next: Check the oil every fill-up and top it off. Owners report less burning on full synthetic. Have any external leaks fixed.

issues.t: Valve cover gasket oil leak
issues.sym: Oil seeping around the top of the engine, a burning oil smell, or oil loss that looks like burning.
issues.why: The valve cover gaskets and spark plug tube seals harden and leak with age and miles.
issues.next: Have the leak confirmed. Replace the valve cover gaskets along with the spark plug tube seals.

issues.t: Check engine light from the air injection pump
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with a secondary air injection code. You may hear the pump whine or not run at all on a cold start.
issues.why: The secondary air injection (smog) pump blows extra air into the exhaust for the first minute after a cold start. The pump or its valve fails on these engines.
issues.next: The car still drives normally, but it may fail an emissions test. Have the pump, check valve and hoses tested before replacing parts.

issues.t: Oil can drip onto the exhaust and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning oil smell from under the hood, or in the worst case a small engine fire.
issues.why: Oil from the front valve cover area can drip onto the hot exhaust manifold and ignite. GM recalled these cars more than once (NHTSA 09V116 and 15V701) to install an improved valve cover and gasket.
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN for open recall work. Until it's done, GM advised parking outside.

issues.t: Heater hose can rub and leak onto the exhaust (recall)
issues.sym: Coolant smell or steam from under the hood, or a falling coolant level.
issues.why: Some cars were built without a heater hose clip, so the hose could sag against the oxygen sensor and leak coolant onto the hot exhaust. GM recalled them (NHTSA 98V241).
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN; the fix is a free clip.

issues.t: Rear seat belt may be unusable (recall)
issues.sym: A rear seat belt can't be buckled or pulled out properly.
issues.why: The rear seat belt system could become unusable, leaving a passenger unbelted. GM recalled these cars (NHTSA 00V044).
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN for this recall.

issues.t: Rear seat belt buckles may not hold (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom in normal use.
issues.why: Some TRW buckle bases were not heat treated correctly and may not hold in a crash. GM recalled affected cars (NHTSA 00V228).
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN; they check the buckle date codes and replace affected buckles.

issues.t: ABS unit can leak internally (recall)
issues.sym: ABS, traction control or brake warning lights, or the car not braking evenly in hard stops.
issues.why: Some cars built in January 2000 had internal leaks in the brake hydraulic control unit, so rear brake proportioning, ABS or traction control may not work right. GM recalled them (NHTSA 00V114).
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN; the fix is an inspection and new ABS modulator if needed.

issues.t: Ignition switch can slip out of Run (recall)
issues.sym: The engine can shut off while driving if the key is bumped or the key ring is heavy.
issues.why: The ignition can move out of Run, and then the airbags may not deploy in a crash. This is part of GM's 2014 ignition switch recall (NHTSA 14V400).
issues.next: Have a GM dealer check your VIN. Until then, carry only the ignition key with nothing heavy on it.

issues.t: Replacement headlamps may not aim correctly (recall)
issues.sym: Headlights aim too high or too low after a headlamp assembly was replaced.
issues.why: Some replacement headlamp assemblies could not be aimed correctly, which breaks federal lighting rules. GM recalled them (NHTSA 98V102/98V103).
issues.next: If your headlights seem misaimed, have a dealer check your VIN for this recall.

issues.t: Won't start with the security light flashing
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't start, or won't start at all, with the security light on or flashing. It may clear up after 10 to 30 minutes.
issues.why: The anti-theft system blocks starting when it can't confirm the key, usually from a worn ignition switch, sensor or module.
issues.next: Try leaving the key in On for about 10 minutes until the security light stops flashing, then restart. If it keeps happening, have the anti-theft system and ignition switch diagnosed.

issues.t: Dash lights up and engine shuts off while driving
issues.sym: Every warning light on the dash comes on at once and the engine dies while driving. Afterward it may not restart, sometimes with the security light on.
issues.why: Owners have not pinned down one cause. The security system, ignition switch and body control module are the usual suspects, and parts swapping often fails.
issues.next: Get to a safe spot. Have a shop that knows GM electrical systems scan all modules for codes while the problem is happening, before replacing parts.

issues.t: Power window motor or pulley breaks
issues.sym: A window stops working, moves slowly, or you hear a snap or grinding inside the door. Some owners lose several windows.
issues.why: The window motor and regulator pulley wear out and break.
issues.next: Replace the regulator and motor assembly for that door.

issues.t: Squeal behind the glove box when the fan runs
issues.sym: A high-pitched squeak or squeal from behind the glove box whenever the heater or A/C fan runs. The fan may work only on high.
issues.why: The blower motor and its speed resistor, both under the glove box, wear out.
issues.next: Replace the blower motor and resistor. It is a quick job.

issues.t: Wipers stop in the upright position
issues.sym: The wipers work normally but stop standing up on the windshield when you turn them off.
issues.why: The wiper motor's park function or the linkage fails.
issues.next: Have the wiper motor and linkage checked. Don't drive in rain if the wipers aren't working right.
